title: Questionnaire readiness checklist + sample evidence snippets
body:
Purpose:
This working note is a compact readiness checklist and a set of small, copy-pasteable evidence snippets to help Solutions/CS and Security SMEs respond to customer security questionnaires focused on RBAC v2, audit logs, and SIEM exports. It is intentionally pragmatic: short answers, required artifacts, and sample log lines or export rows that show where evidence lives and what to redact.

Status and scope:
- Draft: intended as a field tool for CS engineers preparing for customer assessments and SOC/third-party audits.
- Scope: RBAC v2 evidence (roles, assignment mapping, change controls), canonical audit log schema, example SIEM export rows, and short answer templates for common questionnaire asks (data residency, retention, redaction, access reviews).

How to use this doc:
- Step 1: Pick the questionnaire section (RBAC / Audit log / SIEM / Retention).
- Step 2: Attach the referenced artifact(s) (policy snapshots, sample logs, Jira change record).
- Step 3: Replace the bracketed placeholders in the sample answers with the customer-specific details (region, retention length, point-of-contact).

Quick readiness checklist (items to gather before customer call):
- RBAC policy export (RBAC v2 JSON dump) and human-readable role matrix (CSV) showing role -> permissions -> owner.
- Two recent access review outputs (report showing users removed or confirmed).
- Change history for role definitions (audit trail / PR link / Jira change request).
- Representative audit log extract (ndjson) covering a 24-hour window including: role changes, token issuance, and admin actions.
- SIEM export sample (CSV or syslog lines) demonstrating field mapping and timestamp normalization.
- Evidence mapping doc: short table pointing each questionnaire question to artifact(s) and page/line reference.
- Redaction policy summary and sample redacted artifact.

Sample evidence snippets (copy/paste friendly)
1) RBAC v2 human summary (one-paragraph):
"RBAC v2 is our canonical authorization model in the control plane. Roles are defined as permission sets and versioned in git under infra/rbac/v2. Each role has an owner in the product-security or platform-eng group. Assignments are made through our identity service and recorded in the identity-index database; changes require a PR with an approver from the role owner. We retain role-change records for 7 years per our retention policy (see linked policy)."

2) Short answer template: "How are role changes authorized and reviewed?"
"Role changes follow RBAC v2 workflow: author creates a role-edit PR tracked in Jira [JIRA-XXXX], two approvers required (role owner + security reviewer). The PR triggers an automated test suite and a policy-change audit-entry is created when merged (audit_event=role.update, logged to audit.log). Quarterly access reviews are scheduled and results are stored in Confluence under Security > Access Reviews."

3) Minimum artifact list to attach for RBAC questions:
- rbac-v2-export-2026-02-14.json (redacted)
- rbac-role-matrix-2026Q1.csv (role -> permission matrix)
- jira-PR-1459-role-change.pdf (change approval proof)

Canonical audit log schema (short reference):
- field: event_id (uuid) -- unique event id
- field: ts (ISO8601) -- event timestamp in UTC
- field: principal_id (string) -- internal user id or service account id
- field: principal_type (user|service|api_key)
- field: action (string) -- high level action (e.g., auth.token.issue, role.update, model.deploy, secret.access)
- field: resource (string) -- resource path (e.g., /models/gs-13b/versions/2)
- field: outcome (success|failure)
- field: ip (ipaddr) -- source IP (redacted in customer extracts where required)
- field: request_id (uuid) -- correlation id
- field: metadata (json-string) -- free-form details (limited to non-sensitive keys)

Sample ndjson audit log extract (3 lines):
{"event_id":"e29b3a7c-4f6a-4d2b-9b7a-1a2f8b4c1234","ts":"2026-02-12T14:03:22Z","principal_id":"svc-deploy-01","principal_type":"service","action":"model.deploy","resource":"/models/gh-7b/versions/12","outcome":"success","ip":"10.1.2.5","request_id":"req-8f7a","metadata":"{"node":"gpu-3","duration_ms":312}"}
{"event_id":"31f7a9b0-9a4c-43a4-b1ee-bcf8aa5566d2","ts":"2026-02-12T14:05:01Z","principal_id":"alice.lee@redwood.com","principal_type":"user","action":"role.update","resource":"/rbac/roles/observer","outcome":"success","ip":"REDACTED","request_id":"req-9b2c","metadata":"{"changes":"added permission logs.read"}"}
{"event_id":"b81ff4e1-2c2a-4f90-9bde-0cc9f2d5f00c","ts":"2026-02-12T15:10:11Z","principal_id":"api-key-09","principal_type":"api_key","action":"auth.token.issue","resource":"/tokens","outcome":"success","ip":"REDACTED","request_id":"req-67a1","metadata":"{"expires_in":3600}"}

Notes on redaction for customer extracts:
- IPs: replace external IP with REDACTED unless customer NDA permits full IPs. Internal/overlay addresses may be left as-is if clearly labelled internal.
- Personal identifiers: convert full emails to hashed or REDACTED when not required for the ask. Example: alice.lee@redwood.com -> alice.lee@REDACTED or hash: sha256:abcd...
- Metadata: remove secrets, full resource payloads, and any PII fields. Keep schema keys so auditors can validate structure.

SIEM export examples and field mapping (compact):
- Standard outgoing format: ndjson per line or CSV with header.
- Minimal customer CSV header map we supply: timestamp,event_id,principal_type,principal_id,action,resource,outcome,ip,request_id,metadata

Example CSV row (comma-escaped metadata):
2026-02-12T14:03:22Z,e29b3a7c-4f6a-4d2b-9b7a-1a2f8b4c1234,service,svc-deploy-01,model.deploy,/models/gh-7b/versions/12,success,10.1.2.5,req-8f7a,"{"node":"gpu-3","duration_ms":312}"

Mapping notes for common SIEM columns:
- timestamp -> ts (convert to UTC if local)
- user field -> principal_id; when sending to customer SIEM, we can map internal ids to email aliases if requested and authorized.
- resource -> normalised path for easier rule writing (we can provide regex helpers).

Sample short answers for common questionnaire items (fill and attach artifacts):
Q: "Do you provide a raw audit log export suitable for SIEM ingestion?"
A: "Yes. We provide ndjson and CSV exports of audit events on request. Exports include our canonical fields (timestamp, event_id, principal, action, resource, outcome, request_id, metadata). Sensitive fields are redacted according to our evidence-redaction-policy. Typical delivery is a 7-day rolling export or an ad-hoc 24-hour slice delivered via a secure transfer link."

Q: "How long are audit logs retained and how do you support legal hold?"
A: "Default retention for audit logs is 3 years in hot storage and 7 years in cold archive. For customers who require longer retention or legal hold, we support bespoke retention exports and can configure a dedicated export pipeline as part of Dedicated or Private deployments. Evidence of retention is provided by storage policy snapshots and sample export receipts (attached)."

Q: "How do you prove that role changes were approved?"
A: "Every change to RBAC v2 role definitions is tracked in source control. A PR shows the diff, approvers, timestamps, and an automated policy test run. We attach the PR (or PDF export) and the merge commit as proof. See attached 'jira-PR-1459-role-change.pdf' and the policy-change audit entry from audit.log (event.action=role.update, request_id=req-9b2c)."

Evidence automation tips for CS/SME working a questionnaire:
- Use the evidence map: one-row per question listing: question id, short answer, artifact name, file path in Drive/Confluence, and redaction note. Keep this map as the single artifact you hand to the customer.
- Automate exports: we have a small script (infra/scripts/export-audit-slice.sh) that outputs ndjson and CSV slices for a given date range. If a customer requests an export, run the script, apply the redaction tool, and store the result in a secure transfer bucket.
- Reuse standard answers: keep a short templates doc for yes/no + 1-paragraph elaboration. Attach the minimal evidence; avoid over-sharing raw internal logs.

Operational contacts and escalation:
- First-line: Solutions Engineering (SE) assigned to account.
- Security SME: Samantha Lee (samantha.lee@redwood.com)
- Audit export ops: platform-ops@redwood.com
- SLA for ad-hoc export requests: 3 business days for standard 24h slices; expedited available under contract.

Open questions / TODOs for product/security owners (internal):
- Confirm canonical retention numbers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes and add table (Hosted: 3y hot / 7y cold; Dedicated: customer-configurable; Private: customer-managed).
- Provide a sanitized example of a full 7-day export for marketing reuse.
- Add a brief how-to for mapping our principal_id to customer-facing email aliases for exports when the customer requires email mapping.

Appendix: quick copy templates (attach artifacts when sending)
- Email subject: "Security evidence for [Customer] — RBAC & Audit Logs"
- Email body (short): "Attached: RBAC v2 role matrix (redacted), sample audit-log slice (ndjson), PR proof for recent role change, access review report. See also our evidence map (attached). Contact Security SME Samantha Lee for questions."

End of doc.

Notes: this is a working draft. Prefer short, concrete artifacts over long narrated documents when responding to customer questionnaires.
